chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadalah, from Abu al-Mi'za, from Abu Basir, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man ended his ihram (state of consecration for Hajj) but his wife had not ended hers, so he had intercourse with her. He said: 'Upon her is a camel (as expiation), which her husband must pay for.'

key_terms.إِحْرَام: State of consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.يَغْرَمُهَا: He bears the cost/pays for it

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for a husband who has intercourse with his wife after he ended his ihram but she did not?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this narration clarifies the asymmetry in expiation when a husband ends his ihram before his wife; the husband bears the financial burden of the *badanah* (a specific type of camel or its monetary equivalent) as compensation. This ruling highlights the principle that the husband’s early termination of the ritual state invalidates the joint sanctity of the act, making him liable for the penalty even if the wife remains in the sacred state. It serves as a key precedent in Shia jurisprudence for calculating *kaffarah* in mixed-status marital relations during Hajj.
